cards.heading: Three owned layers
cards.question: What three layers make up the LLM wiki architecture?
cards.answer: Immutable raw sources the model reads but never edits; a wiki of model-generated interlinked markdown pages the model owns entirely; and a schema document (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md-style) encoding structure, conventions and workflows.

cards.heading: Lint operation
cards.question: What does the periodic "lint" operation check for in the LLM wiki architecture?
cards.answer: Contradictions, superseded claims, orphan pages, concepts lacking pages, and missing cross-references.

cards.heading: Ingest integrates, not indexes
cards.question: What does "ingest" do beyond simply indexing a new source for later retrieval?
cards.answer: It integrates the source into the wiki: writing a summary page, updating the index, and revising the entity and concept pages the source touches — often 10-15 pages per source.

cards.heading: Query and filing back
cards.question: How does the query operation work, and what happens to a good answer afterward?
cards.answer: It reads the index first, drills into relevant pages, and synthesizes a cited answer; answers worth keeping are filed back into the wiki as pages, so exploration compounds like ingestion does.

cards.heading: Navigation: index.md vs log.md
cards.question: What are index.md and log.md for in the LLM wiki architecture?
cards.answer: index.md is a categorized catalog updated on every ingest and read first at query time — enough for roughly a hundred sources without embedding-based retrieval. log.md is an append-only, grep-parseable timeline of ingests, queries and lint passes.

cards.heading: Economic rationale
cards.question: Why does this architecture claim to avoid the usual reason human-maintained wikis get abandoned?
cards.answer: Humans abandon wikis because bookkeeping grows faster than value; moving the summarizing, filing and consistency work to the model prices maintenance near zero, leaving humans to source, direct and question.
